footnote: VM/core mapping is the five-VM image's PLAN (VM k = guest k−1). Times are from each run's first record. Timestamps are Arm generic timer counts (EL2 reads the physical count, the guests the virtual count); the START record gives 1 GHz, so one count is 1 ns, and the recorded values move in steps of 50 ns.
boundary: Block edges are where the records were taken, a little inside the real transitions. An EL2 block starts after the exception entry and the entry stub (which saves the guest's registers) and ends before the EL2_EXIT record is written, the exit stub runs and eret returns; those parts are drawn as EL1 and not measured separately. Writing one record in EL2 takes about 0.3–0.4 µs (ETR, 2026-11-23), so this is not negligible. The counter moves in 50 ns steps.
